newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-CANADA GETS REVENGE WITH WIN OVER U.S.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-CANADA GETS REVENGE WITH WIN OVER U.S.

text.p: Canada scored early in the first period then rode the goaltending of Sean Burke to a 5-1 revenge win over the United States at the ice hockey world championships on Thursday.
The victory improved Canada's record to 2-1-1 but still left them third in the B pool standings, one point behind the United States and Sweden.

It was the first loss for the United States, who have not beaten Canada in world championship competition since 1985. But they did defeat their northern rivals in the final of last September's inaugural World Cup.
"We have a tendency to bring out the best in the Canadians," U.S. coach Jeff Jackson said. "I thought they played very well, their best game so far."

With the Americans looking for their first world title in 64 years and the Canadians seeking revenge,it was an entertaining hard-hitting NHL type contest before the first sellout of the tournament in Turku.
"It seems that Canada-U.S. games now, at whatever level they're played, have pushed the competition level," Canadian coach Andy Murray said.
"When the game was 3-1 in the third period I think there was still doubt in people's minds what the outcome would be."
Canada took a 1-0 lead just 1:22 into the first period on a goal by Rob Zamuner of the Tampa Bay Lightning.
The United States had chances to level the score when Canadian captain Dean Evason took a double-minor penalty for high-sticking Dan Plante.
But the Americans were unable to capitalize on that or on any of their six man-advantage situations.
With just over a minute remaining in the second period, Jeff Friesen of the San Jose Sharks put Canada up 2-0.
Benefitting from a lucky bounce, Friesen tapped the game winner into a gaping U.S. net after Mark Recchi's slapshot had richochetted off the goalpost directly onto his stick.
Anson Carter increased Canada's advantage 3-0 before Ken Klee ruined Burke's shutout bid when he blasted a slapshot past the partially screened netminder.
Owen Nolan and Travis Green had the other Canadian goals.
Burke, was solid in the Canadian stopping all but one of the 31 shots directed at him.
